### God Blesses Messy People
Author: Erik Raymond
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/blogs/erik-raymond/god-blesses-messy-people/
Passage: Genesis 26:6-11
Points:
- Scripture openly displays the messiness of its central figures to magnify God's mercy rather than human virtue.
- Driven by fear of the locals rather than trust in God, Isaac repeats his father's sin by claiming Rebekah is his sister.
- A pagan king discovers the deception and rebukes Isaac for exposing his subjects to moral peril and guilt.
- Instead of executing judgment, God intervenes through Abimelech's royal protection to shield Isaac and Rebekah.
- Self-inflicted trials show believers that God's blessings stem from unearned grace rather than human perfection.

### The Lord Favors Isaac
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/lord-favors-isaac
Passage: Genesis 26:6-16
Points:
- Isaac stumbles into the same fear-driven deceit as his father by lying about his marriage to Rebekah.
- Choosing fear over faith jeopardizes the fullness of God's promised covenant blessings.
- Dishonesty motivated by self-preservation puts others in spiritual danger, as Abimelech rightly warned.
- God graciously intervenes to protect His flawed people even when they make foolish, sinful choices.
- Believers are called to confess their fears openly, trusting that God redeems weak servants for His glory.
